countermeasure_tested: f005_liquidity_guard (agents/phase3_7/f005_liquidity_guard.py) -- early cash-trajectory guard: if cash < $200 by day 2, halve the crop portfolio's tile commitment for subsequent planting.
derivation: Directly derived from Stage B's root-cause finding (recovery-failure via tile-survival chance, not over-investment per se) -- the ONE architecturally available lever (reduce future planting before it happens) rather than a lever the project's frozen code doesn't expose.

seed_852025866_vs_passive.note: guard never fired -- cash at day 2 was $572, above the $200 threshold

why_it_failed_to_even_trigger: Cash does not visibly enter crisis territory (near $0) until day 4-6 in this episode's trajectory -- by day 2 it is merely somewhat depleted ($572), indistinguishable from what a normal, ultimately-recoverable episode's day-2 cash level looks like (per Phase 3.4/3.5's own prior documentation: nearly every episode shows a $0-30 cash trough around days 3-10 regardless of eventual outcome). By the time cash is unambiguously in crisis (day 4+), the crop commitment (~21-22 tiles) is ALREADY fully planted -- the intervention window closes before the signal becomes distinguishable from normal variance.
conclusion: REJECTED as designed. This is not a parameter-tuning failure to iterate past -- it is a structural problem: the leading indicator (early cash level) does not discriminate between 'this will recover' and 'this will not' early enough to act, because EVERY episode's early cash trajectory looks similar. A viable countermeasure would need either (a) a different, earlier-discriminating signal not yet identified, or (b) the ability to act on ALREADY-PLANTED tiles (e.g. reduce their number retroactively), which is not available through the external config-mutation pattern this project has used since Phase 3.3.
final_status: NO VIABLE COUNTERMEASURE IDENTIFIED THIS PHASE. F-005 remains NOT SOLVED. Not force-fit into a false 'partial fix'.
side_effect_testing: Not performed -- the guard never activates in the tested scenarios, so there is nothing to check for side effects against normal play; testing it against a scenario engineered to force activation would not represent real conditions (per the finding above, real activation timing/threshold cannot be reliably distinguished from normal variance).
